1) Background of 'Nil Darpan':

o 'Nil Darpan' is a Bengali play written in 1860 by Dinabandhu Mitra.

o It portrays the plight of Indian farmers who were forced into cultivating indigo under oppressive conditions by British planters.

2) Historical Significance:

o The play became a crucial tool for awakening public opinion against British exploitation.

o It was later translated into English by Rev. James Long, leading to Long's imprisonment by the British government.

Incorrect options:

· Motilal Nehru: A prominent Indian leader, but not associated with literary works like 'Nil Darpan.'

· Chittaranjan Das: A lawyer and freedom fighter, known for his political contributions, not for writing this play.

· Sarojini Naidu: Renowned poet and political leader, but unrelated to this work.

Mahasweta devi is the author of the book 'HazaarChaurasi ki Maa'. Mahasweta Devi was an Indian writer in Bengali and an activist. Her notable literary works include Hajar Churashir Maa, Rudali, and Aranyer Adhikar.

Jaishankar Prasad was a prominent figure in modern Hindi literature as well as Hindi theatre. Prasad was his pen name. He was also known as Chhayavadi poet. Kamayani and "Ansu" are his famous works.

Kamayani literally means 'the daughter of Kama'. In Indian literature Kama denotes something more than a mere libido-sense. As Vincent Smith has rightly pointed out, it bears a combined meaning of Libido and Eros of the Greek mythology
Rangbhoomi: The Arena of Life is a Hindi language novel by Premchand. The novel features an idealist protagonist inspired by Gandhian values.

Tarabai Shinde was a prominent social reformer in 19th century India, and she is the author of the groundbreaking work 'Stree Purush Tulana' (A Comparison Between Women and Men). This work was one of the earliest to criticize the oppression of women in Indian society, focusing on the inequalities between men and women.

The author of the book 'The Indian Struggle' is Subhas Chandra Bose.

This book, published in 1935, is an autobiographical account of India's struggle for independence from British rule. It focuses on the period from the First War of Indian Independence in 1857 to the year 1942, and offers insights into Bose's views on the Indian freedom movement.

The Philosophy of the Bomb - This was a revolutionary pamphlet written in response to Gandhis criticism of revolutionary violence.

Bandi Jiwan - This is an autobiographical account by Sachindranath Sanyal, a key revolutionary leader, written during his imprisonment.

Pather Dabi - This Bengali novel had strong political themes and was even banned by the British Government.

Anandmath - Famous for introducing the patriotic song "Vande Mataram", this book is set during the Sannyasi Rebellion.
William Dalrymple's new book, The Anarchy - of how a commercial company ended up controlling a vast empire.

The Great Gatsby, third novel by F. Scott Fitzgerald, published in 1925 by Charles Scribner's Sons. Set in Jazz Age New York, the novel tells the tragic story of Jay Gatsby, a self-made millionaire, and his pursuit of Daisy Buchanan, a wealthy young woman whom he loved in his youth. Unsuccessful upon publication, the book is now considered a classic of American fiction and has often been called the Great American Novel.

The book "The Feast of Roses" is written by Indu Sundaresan in 2008. It is the second novel in her Taj Mahal trilogy, which tells the story of Mehrunnisa, also known as Empress Nur Jahan, the wife of Mughal Emperor Jahangir.

In his book 'The Coalition Years', former president Pranab Mukherjee, had disfavoured the Congress' 2003 decision to forge alliances to defeat the BJP in the 2004 general elections.

The Coalition Years begins its journey in 1996 and explores the highs and lows that characterized sixteen years of one of the most tumultuous periods in the nation's political history. It is an insightful account of the larger governance phenomenon in India - coalition politics - as seen through the eyes of one of the chief architects of the post-Congress era of Indian politics.

Author Pranab Mukherjee was the 13th President of India. A man of unparalleled experience in governance, he has the rare distinction of having served at different times as Foreign, Defence, Commerce and Finance Minister.
